text: The Patriots face the Steelers this week dealing with some notable roster shuffling: cornerback Carlton Davis III has been downgraded to out, forcing the team to navigate secondary coverage against a Pittsburgh offense already missing starting wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. to a foot injury, while running back TreVeyon Henderson—who sat out the opener with an ankle injury—declared himself "ready to go" and is expected to return to bolster the ground game. On the brighter side, the organization found a moment for reflection and reverence when Stephon Gilmore, the 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year and two-time All-Pro who became one of the greatest cornerbacks in franchise history during his New England tenure, signed a one-day contract to retire as a Patriot on Friday. The team elevated punter Mitch Wishnowsky from the practice squad for the second consecutive week, and off the field, owner Robert Kraft made headlines by explaining his decision to remove Macklemore as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's Gillette Stadium shows, citing concerns over "a history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community."
